arxiv-1709-04207.title: Direct top-quark decay width measurement in the 𝐭 ​ 𝐭 ¯ \mathbf{\boldsymbol{t\bar{t}}} lepton+jets channel at s = 8 ​ TeV \sqrt{s}=8\penalty\ \text{TeV} with the ATLAS experiment
arxiv-1709-04207.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-1709-04207.description: Abstract This paper presents a direct measurement of the decay width of the top quark using t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} events in the lepton+jets final state. The data sample was collected by the ATLAS detector at the LHC in proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 8 TeV and corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 20.2 fb -1 .

arxiv-2105-06800.title: A new approach to space-time boundary integral equations for the wave equation
arxiv-2105-06800.creator: Olaf Steinbach, Carolina Urzúa-Torres
arxiv-2105-06800.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Olaf Steinbach, Carolina Urzúa-Torres. We present a new approach for boundary integral equations for the wave equation with zero initial conditions. Unlike previous attempts, our mathematical formulation allows us to prove that the associated boundary integral operators are continuous and satisfy inf-sup conditions in trace spaces of the same regularity, which are closely related to standard energy spaces with the expected regularity in space and time.

arxiv-2207-05581.title: Breaking of internal waves parametrically excited by ageostrophic anticyclonic instability
arxiv-2207-05581.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . A gradient-wind balanced flow with an elliptic streamline parametrically excites internal inertia-gravity waves through ageostrophic anticyclonic instability (AAI). This study numerically investigates the breaking of internal waves and the following turbulence generation resulting from the AAI. In our simulation, we periodically distort the calculation domain following the streamlines of an elliptic vortex and integrate the equations of motion using a Fourier spectral method.

arxiv-2208-00992.title: A study on the Clustering Properties of Radio-Selected sources in the Lockman Hole Region at 325 MHz 2015 A study on the Clustering Properties of Radio-Selected sources in the Lockman Hole Region at 325 MHz – References
arxiv-2208-00992.creator: Aishrila Mazumder, Arnab Chakraborty, Abhirup Datta
arxiv-2208-00992.description: Abstract Studying the spatial distribution of extragalactic source populations is vital in understanding the matter distribution in the Universe. It also enables understanding the cosmological evolution of dark matter density fields and the relationship between dark matter and luminous matter. Clustering studies are also required for EoR foreground studies since it affects the relevant angular scales.

arxiv-2307-13644.title: Manifestly Covariant Worldline Actions from Coadjoint Orbits Part I: Generalities and Vectorial Descriptions
arxiv-2307-13644.creator: TaeHwan OH
arxiv-2307-13644.description: Abstract We derive manifestly covariant actions of spinning particles starting from coadjoint orbits of isometry groups, by using Hamiltonian reductions. We show that the defining conditions of a classical Lie group can be treated as Hamiltonian constraints which generate the coadjoint orbits of another, dual , Lie group.

arxiv-2310-10007.title: Broadband radio study of the North Polar Spur: Origin of the spectral turnover with insights into the X-ray and Gamma-ray spectra
arxiv-2310-10007.creator: Ryoji Iwashita, Jun Kataoka, Yoshiaki Sofue
arxiv-2310-10007.description: Abstract The North Polar Spur (NPS) is a giant structure that is clearly visible in both radio and X-ray all-sky maps. We analyzed broadband radio observations covering a range between 22 MHz and 70 GHz to systematically analyze the thermal/non-thermal emissions associated with the NPS.

arxiv-2402-14139.title: NeuroFlux : Memory-Efficient CNN Training Using Adaptive Local Learning Conference: ; April 22–25, 2024; Athens, Greece EuroSys ’24
arxiv-2402-14139.creator: Dhananjay Saikumar, Blesson Varghese
arxiv-2402-14139.description: Abstract . Efficient on-device Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) training in resource-constrained mobile and edge environments is an open challenge. Backpropagation is the standard approach adopted, but it is GPU memory intensive due to its strong inter-layer dependencies that demand intermediate activations across the entire CNN model to be retained in GPU memory.

arxiv-2405-04704.title: System Identification of the Upgraded LHPOST6 Reaction Mass at the University of California San Diego
arxiv-2405-04704.creator: Andres Rodriguez-Burneo, Jose I. Restrepo, Joel P. Conte
arxiv-2405-04704.description: Abstract \justify Upon completing the upgrade from one to six degrees of freedom of the Outdoor Shake Table at UCSD in 2019, forced vibration tests were carried out to identify the dynamic characteristics of the reaction mass and soil system.

arxiv-2505-19808.title: Quantum computing of magnetic-skyrmion-like patterns in Heisenberg ferromagnets
arxiv-2505-19808.creator: Matej Komelj, Vinko Sršan, Kristina Žužek, Sašo Šturm
arxiv-2505-19808.description: Abstract We diagonalize the quantum two-dimensional spin-1/2 Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) by applying the variational quantum eigensolver, running on a quantum-computer simulator, which turns out to be a more efficient approach than a classical direct diagonalization for systems with more than 17 sites.

arxiv-2510-23641.title: Spatially Aware Linear Transformer (SAL-T) for Particle Jet Tagging
arxiv-2510-23641.creator: Aaron Wang, Zihan Zhao, Subash Katel, Vivekanand Gyanchand Sahu, Elham E Khoda, Abhijith Gandrakota, Jennifer Ngadiuba, Richard Cavanaugh, Javier Duarte
arxiv-2510-23641.description: Abstract Transformers are very effective in capturing both global and local correlations within high-energy particle collisions, but they present deployment challenges in high-data-throughput environments, such as the CERN LHC. The quadratic complexity of transformer models demands substantial resources and increases latency during inference.

pmc-10477156.title: Laparoscopic intervention for late-onset perforating peritonitis due to a ventriculoperitoneal shunt: a case report and literature review
pmc-10477156.creator: Takeshi Morinaga, Osamu Nakahara, Akira Tsuji, Kunitaka Kuramoto, Masayoshi Iizaka, Shintaro Hayashida, Yuki Ohya, Yasuyuki Hitoshi, Yukihiro Inomata
pmc-10477156.description: BackgroundVentriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt placement is commonly performed to treat hydrocephalus and complications are not uncommon. We report here a case of generalized peritonitis caused by migration of the abdominal end of a VP shunt catheter into the bowel after multiple VP shunt revisions over 30 years.

pmc-10673150.title: The Hydrolytic Activity of Copper(II) Complexes with 1,4,7-Triazacyclononane Derivatives for the Hydrolysis of Phosphate Diesters
pmc-10673150.creator: Michaela Buziková, Robert Willimetz, Jan Kotek, Bing Hu
pmc-10673150.description: A set of substituted 1,4,7-triazacyclononane ligands was synthesised, including a wide series of novel derivatives bearing a thiazole or thiophene side group, with the potential to incorporate these derivatives into a polymeric material; some previously known/studied ligands were also synthesised for comparative purposes.

pmc-11347173.title: Nuclear F-actin assembly on damaged chromatin is regulated by DYRK1A and Spir1 phosphorylation
pmc-11347173.creator: Junshi Li, Nan Xiong, Kirk L West, Manton Leung, Yick Pang Ching, Jun Huang, Jian Yuan, Cheng-Han Yu, Justin Leung, Michael Huen
pmc-11347173.description: Nuclear actin-based movements support DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair. However, molecular determinants that promote filamentous actin (F-actin) formation on the damaged chromatin remain undefined. Here we describe the DYRK1A kinase as a nuclear activity that promotes local F-actin assembly to support DSB mobility and repair, accomplished in part by its targeting of actin nucleator spire homolog 1 (Spir1).

pmc-12290582.title: Fast frequency modulation is encoded according to the listener expectations in the human subcortical auditory pathway
pmc-12290582.creator: Alejandro Tabas, Stefan Kiebel, Michael Marxen, Katharina von Kriegstein
pmc-12290582.description: Expectations aid and bias our perception. For instance, expected words are easier to recognise than unexpected words, particularly in noisy environments, and incorrect expectations can make us misunderstand our conversational partner. Expectations are combined with the output from the sensory pathways to form representations of auditory objects in the cerebral cortex.

pmc-12404299.title: Association of short-chain fatty acid–producing gut microbiota and dietary habits with maternal depression in a subclinical population
pmc-12404299.creator: Michiko Matsunaga, Mariko Takeuchi, Satoshi Watanabe, Aya K Takeda, Keisuke Hagihara, Masako Myowa
pmc-12404299.description: The prevalence of postpartum mental illness is steadily increasing, a tendency that was exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Recent studies show that maternal depression is no longer confined to the perinatal period, and this necessitates long-term assessment and support for maternal mental health.

pmc-12620228.title: The effects of cinnamon on patients with metabolic diseases: an umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials
pmc-12620228.creator: Haobo Gou, Ling Zhong, Qiuya Wei, Yong Fan
pmc-12620228.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionAnimal and clinical studies have demonstrated a range of potential health benefits associated with cinnamon. However, its effects on metabolic parameters such as blood glucose, blood pressure, lipid profiles, and body weight in patients with metabolic diseases remain controversial.

pmc-12752154.title: Urine-based nematode chemotaxis assay (N-NOSE) as a predictor of recurrence after curative surgery for resectable pancreatic cancer: preliminary data and single center experience
pmc-12752154.creator: Masahiro Fukada, Noriki Mitsui, Takeshi Horaguchi, Itaru Yasufuku, Yuta Sato, Jesse Yu Tajima, Yoshihiro Tanaka, Hideyuki Hatakeyama, Aya Hasan Alshammari, Masayo Morishita, Takaaki Hirotsu, Eric di Luccio, Manabu Futamura, Nobuhisa Matsuhashi
pmc-12752154.description: BackgroundPancreatic cancer (PC) remains one of the most lethal malignancies, with high recurrence rates even after curative-intent surgery. Current surveillance tools, including imaging and serum carbohydrate antigen 19–9, have limitations in specificity and sensitivity. N-NOSE is a urine-based assay using the chemotactic behavior of Caenorhabditis elegans to detect cancer-associated volatile organic compounds.

pmc-12824190.title: Recovery of iron from iron tailings by co-pyrolysis with coal gangue: process optimization and economic evaluation
pmc-12824190.creator: Zheng Liu, Fengxing Zhang, Guanling Zheng
pmc-12824190.description: Iron tailings and coal gangue are voluminous solid waste byproducts. However, traditional disposal methods and conventional reduction roasting often are hindered by high costs and a reliance on external fossil fuels as reductants. To overcome these challenges, this study introduces a novel co-pyrolysis process utilizing coal gangue as the sole reductant source for recovering iron from tailings.

pmc-13592539.title: The Effectiveness of a Prenatal Educational Programme on Fear of Childbirth Among Primigravida Women: A quasi-experimental pretest–post-test study
pmc-13592539.creator: Mozah Al Mamari, Amal Al Hadi, Fahima Al Harthy, Shamsa Al Ghusaini, Kadhiya Al Riyami
pmc-13592539.description: SummaryObjectives:Fear of childbirth is commonly reported among primigravida women and may negatively influence labour and birth outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured prenatal educational programme in reducing fear of childbirth among primigravida women.Methods:A quasi-experimental single-group pretest-post-test design was conducted from January to June 2025.

pmc-13660261.title: Investigating respiratory infection as a post-COVID-19 condition using a large passive surveillance cohort from Track PCC
pmc-13660261.creator: Marina Oktapodas Feiler, Recai M. Yucel, Bari J. Dzomba, Resa M. Jones
